parts.search_notes: Direct native search of Goldie logarithm laws/reciprocals and Exercise2B, and YM logarithm laws, variable-base simultaneous examples, exponential substitutions, Exercise9 and Revision9. Goldie p46 Reciprocals means log(1/y)=-log y, not reciprocal-base logs. YM Try11(b) is a genuine variable-base lead but solves simultaneous xy=81 and log_x(y)=3; it does not provide the target reciprocal pair. This is a bounded no-match, not an exhaustive absence claim.
parts.reason: No reciprocal-log/change-of-base pure-square counterpart was found in the stated directly inspected pages. For exam log(y)/log(5)=4log(5)/log(y), cross multiplication gives(log y)²=4(log5)², so both signed log values survive and y=25 or1/25 (y>0, y!=1). Goldie2B10(ii) instead needs three-term quadratic factorisation, rejects the negative root of positive 5^x, and takes logs to recover x. These are three substantive method changes, so remove the previous structural-branch link.

closest_items_rejected.reason: Three method differences: factor u²+u-2 rather than take both signs of a pure square; reject u=-2 because u=5^x>0 rather than retain both signed logarithms; take logs to recover exponent x rather than exponentiate to recover y. Both are nonlinear equations, but that does not make them one ordered branch.

YM416 variable-base simultaneous system xy=81 and log_x(y)=3 requires y=x³ then x⁴=81 and a positive-base filter. It neither cross-multiplies reciprocal logarithms nor keeps two signed logarithm roots.
